objective: Implement the pure domain layer: money, time, canonical, compat, planner with brute-force oracle, state tables, rescue-status derivation (revision 2) and explanation templates, with the fixture and the unit, property and timing tests of the plan.
context: Built against the architecture brief (RS-FIX-1, planner rules, state machines, derivation, RS-06..RS-11, RS-36, NFR5) and the design spec (internal module contracts, Rescue status derivation revision 2 rows 1-14 incl. 4a/5a, Testing Strategy). The reference model .eccode/drafts/design-r2-derive-walk.mjs and the reviewer scripts tr-design-r2-derive.mjs / tr-design-derive-totality.mjs were ported into the tests. Memory search for planner, derivation and oracle returned no records.
expectedOutput: src/domain/{money,time,canonical,compat,planner,oracle,states,derive,explain}.js, test/fixtures/rs-fix-1.json, eight domain unit test files and the NFR5 planner timing test, all passing.
acceptanceCriteria: src/domain imports nothing outside src/domain; the clock is injected; equal inputs give deep-equal outputs

RS-06..RS-11 hold exactly as worded in the brief, each in a test named 'RS-0n: ...' in planner-fixture.test.js, including the multiplicity guard (A on_hand 2 -> Ax2 at 7000, 1 pickup) and RS-12's planner half
planner-oracle.property.test.js compares the planner with oracle.js on 500 seeded random catalogs (<= 6 offers, on_hand 0-3) for feasibility, total, pickups, readyAt and the per-candidate codes
states.js holds the four transition tables of the brief and the OQ-D1 reasons; states.test.js checks every allowed and every refused pair; assertTransition throws AppError(409, INVALID_STATE)

derive.js implements the revision-2 table row by row (rows 1-14 incl. 4a, 5a, row-2 clauses (a) and (b), row-3 unknown-refund clause); derive.test.js has table cases for every row, RS-36 (i)-(iv), reviewer scenarios S09-S20 and the totality property test (25,000 walks x 120 events, row 14 never reached)
money.js uses integer cents, basis-point tax rounded half up per supplier order, toPayPalValue without floating point; time.js converts Asia/Amman local times through Intl, not a constant offset
explain.js renders template text from planner and derive codes, including the brief's exact sentences and the server question templates per field (SEC-7)
test/timing/planner-generator.test.js runs RS-FIX-1 and generator seeds 1-200 with the brief's parameters and asserts < 1 s each (NFR5 planner part)
completedWork: All nine domain modules plus src/domain/errors.js (the domain's own AppError(status, code, message, details), name 'AppError') exist and pass 110 tests through the plan's verification command. Planner: exact lexicographic search (total, pickups, plan-ready time, sorted supplier-code string, then multiplicity vector) by branch-and-bound over bundle multiplicities 0..min(availability, ceil(need/units)); candidate filter codes INCOMPATIBLE_LID_DIAMETER, READY_AFTER_DEADLINE, OUT_OF_STOCK, OFFER_WITHDRAWN; infeasible output carries per-candidate codes (INSUFFICIENT_QTY, TOO_MANY_PICKUPS, OVER_BUDGET from the cheapest covering combination), computed relaxations (budget, deadline, maxPickups, each re-solved with only that constraint removed) and blocking constraints; up to 3 irredundant ranked alternatives and trace comparisons. RS-FIX-1 results: A+B 8400/2 pickups/10:30; A on_hand 2 -> Ax2 7000/1 pickup; without B A+E 9500/10:40; budget 9000 -> exactly budget 9500 (A+E) and deadline 11:20 (D, 8000) relaxations; max pickups 1 -> A, B, E coded INSUFFICIENT_QTY + TOO_MANY_PICKUPS. The oracle enumerates every 0..availability vector with no pruning and its own constraint logic; 500 seeded catalogs agree on feasibility, best total/pickups/readyAt/suppliers/bundles, alternatives, rejections, candidate codes, relaxations and blocking. Planner time over RS-FIX-1 and seeds 1-200 is about 1 ms each (limit 1 s). Derive: revision-2 table row by row (rows 1, 2 with clauses (a) and (b), 3 with the unknown-refund clause, 4, 4a, 5, 5a, 6, 7-9 with r2 scoping, 10-13, 14 with fallback flag and state vector), consuming persisted rows with the data-model column names. The totality test runs 20,000 default-profile walks plus 5,000 progress-profile walks of 120 events over the composed plan/reservation/payment/fulfilment machines, void rule, hooks, compensation, re-plan queue, admin refunds and clock jumps; every model move is asserted against states.js, every step is compared with the reference table, RS-36 (i)-(iii) are checked as invariants, rows 1-13, 4a and 5a are all hit and row 14 is never reached. A deliberate mutation of the row-3 unknown-refund clause was caught by three tests and reverted. Other decisions: a planner node cap (MAX_SEARCH_NODES 2,000,000, PlannerLimitError with code PLANNER_LIMIT) guards absurd inputs; offers whose capacity or cup diameter differ from the requirement are skipped and marked SPEC_MISMATCH in the trace only (not in rejections, because the Rejection code enum has no such code); excluded suppliers are dropped silently and recorded in trace.inputs; several offers of one supplier form one supplier order (one pickup, largest prep fee, one tax rounding); the fixture file is pinned by sha256 in planner-fixture.test.js.
remainingIssues: Interface for the services (W4): deriveRescueStatus takes persisted rows with snake_case column names (plan_versions, reservations, supplier_orders incl. an optional joined supplier_code, payment_operations, provider_calls, planning_runs, replan_queue as { failed_drains }); the spec only named the argument groups, so this shape is the contract to build the view service against (documented in the header of src/domain/derive.js). Limits are camelCase: { unknownEscalateMin, pendingEscalateMin, replanFailedDrainsBeforeManual } with defaults 15, 1440, 5.

src/domain/errors.js defines its own AppError (domain may not import src/http). The HTTP envelope must map it by duck typing (err.name === 'AppError', status, code, message, details) or re-export this class; two distinct AppError classes will otherwise not satisfy instanceof.
PlannerLimitError (RangeError, code PLANNER_LIMIT) can be thrown for absurd catalogs; the plans service should map it to a typed 4xx/5xx, not let it surface as an untyped 500.

The brief gives the NFR5 generator no deadline or budget; the generator in test/unit/domain/helpers/catalog-gen.js fixes the deadline at 11:30 and draws the budget from 6000-30000 cents (164 of 200 seeds feasible). If the delivery lead wants other values, change those two lines.

Relaxations are emitted in the order budget, deadline, maxPickups (the brief's listing of constraints); RS-11's text in the brief names TOO_MANY_PICKUPS first, so consumers and tests should look relaxations up by constraint, not by position (the tests do).

The derivation's per-row nextStepCode and messageCode values beyond the spec's exact sentences (for example CAPTURES_IN_PROGRESS, AUTHORIZATION_IN_PROGRESS, APPROVAL_CANCELLED) are my choices within the spec's nextStep code set; texts live in explain.js.
Nothing outside the task's ownership globs was changed. The PreToolUse guard refused one attempt (an inline python3 program that wrote a file); the same edit was then made with the Edit tool.
nextAction: delivery-lead: dispatch the independent reviewer for b2-domain (check derive.js against the revision-2 table row by row, RS-36 inspection item F-TR-9), then unblock the services stream (W4: plans, supersession, reservations, view) that consumes planner.plan, deriveRescueStatus, assertTransition and explain.js.

lessonDecisions.note: appliesWhen: designing or using a hook/guard that maps file writes to a project record or root. This task is pure domain code and never touches guard or root resolution; the guard was only exercised as a user, where every owned write inside the nested record was allowed (no 'has no claimed task' or 'outside the ownership' denial), so the wrong-root symptom did not occur.
